title: Career Advice for Millennials from Robots
main_content:
Almost half of jobs in the United States are likely to be automated within the next 20 years.

That prediction comes from researchers at the University of Oxford in England. They think more and more machines will be given jobs that people traditionally performed.

The workplace has become increasingly dependent on machines. It comes as no surprise that many workers are becoming concerned about the future. Among them are millennials – people who became adults since the year 2000.

Nigel Dessau is a business expert. He was born in England, but now lives in Massachusetts.

Mr. Dessau says there are ways that workers, especially Millennials, can get used to this new, robot-centered reality.

The first, he says, is content.

“So that’s, what do you know? What do you bring, that a machine doesn’t know?”

The next value is approach. By this, he means a way of doing things.

And finally, he says, workers should be directing their attention on their contacts.

“Who knows what you know, and what you can do? Focus more on the content and the ability to work as a team.”

questions.question: Who are millennials?
options: Individuals who became adults since the year 2000
Those who are currently in their twenties
questions.answer: Individuals who became adults since the year 2000

questions.question: What are the three things workers should direct their attention to, according to Nigel Dessau?
options: Technical skills, emotional intelligence, and adaptability

questions.question: Who is Nigel Dessau?
options: A researcher at the University of Oxford
A business expert from England living in Massachusetts
A millennial worker concerned about job security
questions.answer: A business expert from England living in Massachusetts
